name: Documentation steps
description: Operation steps with a numbered vertical axis: Each step has instructions, reproducible code (can be switched by platform), prompts and completion results. Readers can mark completion step by step.
scenarios: Sequential operations such as installation, connection, and deployment
Steps to differentiate commands by platform (macOS/Windows/Linux) or host
Process description from creation to release

boundaries: Use for actions that need to be performed in order; use text lists for concept notes or unsequential points.
The code is only displayed and copied, not executed.

usage.purpose: Let readers complete an operation in order, knowing which step to take at any time and what to see after each step.
structure: On the numbered vertical axis on the left, click the number to mark completion, and the vertical axis will be filled with completion; the completion progress is displayed at the top.
Each step: title, description, code panel (language tab or platform tab + copy button), prompt, checked result row.

inputs.meaning: It is recommended that each set of steps be performed in sequence, no more than 8 steps.
Step title, written as an action, such as "Start local workbench". Inline tags are available.
Description, segmented by line breaks. Inline tags: **bold**,`代码`, [text] (link); links can be written ashttps://…or doc:slug#anchor.
The command or code to be executed; lines starting with # or // appear in comment color.

omission.description: The code panel is not shown when there are no variants.

inputs.meaning: The language label in the upper left corner of the code panel.
Code to switch by platform or host, replacing code when present. 2–4 recommended.
A tab page: tags and corresponding codes.
Tab name, such as macOS, Windows, Codex.
The code displayed on this tab.
Add tips or precautions and weaken the display. Inline tags are available.
What the reader will see when you're done, shown as a result row with a check mark. Inline tags are available.
The number of the first step; used to continue the numbering when splitting a process into multiple sections.

recipes.title: Write installation steps
steps: Only do one thing at each step, and write the action in the title.
Put commands into code; use variants for different platforms.
Use result to write the results that readers should see to facilitate self-checking.

interactions.effect: Switch the completion status of the step, and the vertical axis and progress bar are updated; "Reset" clears everything.

interactions.action: Switch platform labels (direction keys can switch)
interactions.effect: The code panel displays the commands for the corresponding platform.
Copy the current code and display "Copied"; when the environment does not allow copying, select the code and press ⌘C / Ctrl+C.

constraints: The reading operation only changes the local view state and does not modify the page data.
It is recommended that each group should not exceed 8 steps; long codes should be scrolled horizontally and should not be broken.

data: Add and delete steps, modify commands and results.
implementation: Extend the schema and publish a new version when new step fields are added.

entryPoints.purpose: Components, CodePanel, copy logic, md() and readData.
Tokens, vertical axis, code panel and narrow screen rules.

architecture: The completion status is a local boolean array; the vertical axis segments are filled with scaleY of ::after.
To copy, use hidden textarea + execCommand('copy') first. If it fails, use Range to select the code and prompt (the Clipboard API is prohibited in the sandbox).
extensionPoints: isComment() determines the coloring of comment lines.
invariants: The component does not call onChange.
The tab page uses role=tab / tabpanel, and the copy button has Chinese aria-label.
verification: Check out the vertical axis, code panel and results row in 1000px, 390px width and dark theme.
Click the number to switch the completion status; after clicking copy, a "Copied" or selected prompt will be displayed.

steps.title: Prepare for Node.js
steps.body: Running from source requires Git, **Node.js 22.12 or higher**, and npm. Confirm the version first:

variants.label: Linux
variants.code:
# 使用 nvm 安装
nvm install 22
node --version

steps.title: Get the source code and build
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/Renaissance-Mind/ShowAI.git
cd ShowAI
npm ci
npm run build:browser

steps.title: Start local workbench
steps.body: The browser will automatically open after the service is started. **Keep the terminal running during use**.
steps.note: When the browser does not open automatically, copy the address displayed on the terminal; when finished, press `Ctrl+C `to stop the service.
steps.result: The workbench appears in the browser with a list of projects on the left.

steps.title: New project and first page
steps.body: Click "New Project" and create a new Page in the project. Enter `/`to insert a chart, table or component, see [Page and Board](doc:page-board) for details.
steps.result: The save status at the top shows "Saved".

examples.name: Install the plugin in Claude Code

steps.title: Add the plugin market and install it
steps.body: Execute in the ShowAI warehouse directory:
steps.code:
claude plugin marketplace add ./
claude plugin install showai@renaissance-mind

steps.title: Register runtime
steps.body: The standalone runtime built from source code needs to be registered once; the desktop version can view the configuration in "Settings → Connect Agent".
steps.result: The plug-in can find the ShowAI runtime in the content library.
